summary: Configured node1 so datauser is limited to 100 MB by XFS under /srv/data. The quota survived a node reboot and remained actively enforced.
actions_performed: Created datauser and /srv/data with datauser:datauser ownership and mode 0750.
Enabled persistent XFS user quotas on the root filesystem.
Set datauser's soft and hard block limits to 102400 KiB (100 MiB).
Verified over-limit writes fail with Disk quota exceeded.
Rebooted node1 and verified boot identity changed, system health recovered, data persisted, and quota enforcement remained active.

evidence.summary: Final state shows datauser exists, /srv/data is owned by datauser:datauser with mode 0750, and the directory is clean.
XFS accounting and enforcement are ON; datauser has 102400 KiB soft and hard limits; a real over-limit write failed with Disk quota exceeded.
Final evidence shows usrquota active, defaults,uquota in /etc/fstab, rootflags=uquota in kernel arguments, and the system running normally.

Captured healthy baseline at boot ID 69653db8-4543-4b84-b494-4340f76880c3, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID cc770d60-18b2-4b84-b4e3-add9177d8abb, recovered system/data, and successful post-restart enforcement testing.
